transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Start: 10:30 AM UTC
Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Ethan Cole (Redwood SE); Dr. Lina Morales; Samir Rao; Priya Kapoor; Alex Chen
Links shared: prompt-set-v2.xlsx (drive), scorecard-v1.csv (drive), security-deck.pdf (Redwood link: https://redwood.example/security)

Auto-generated summary (opt):
- Focus: root-cause for recent accuracy regressions, prompt surgery plan, and guardrail tuning schedule.
- Immediate ask: Redwood to provide patched prompt-set + scoring baseline; customer to run expanded evals.

Topics: regression signals, prompt-level failure modes, KV cache interactions, fallback playbook, security checklist

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we got about 50 minutes. Quick roll call — Maya from Redwood, Ethan in for the SE portion.
[00:12] Dr. Lina Morales: Hey, thanks, Lina here — sorry, noisy background — good to see y'all.
[00:18] Samir Rao: Samir on my side. We have the results from last weekend's run and, uh, some worrying diffs.
[00:27] Ethan Cole: Cool, can you — quick check — is the scorecard you shared the latest? I have scorecard-v1.csv open.
[00:32] Alex Chen: yes that's the one, although we noted there are two variants, v1-stable and v1-batch, they diverge on long contexts.
[00:40] Priya Kapoor: And security is here, Priya — we will want the KMS notes patched into the doc by next week.
[00:45] Maya Patel: Great — agenda: 1) walk through top regressions, 2) prompt surgery plan, 3) guardrails/fallback, 4) action items.
[00:55] Dr. Lina Morales: I'll share the heatmap quick — highest deltas are on invoice-parsing prompts and a handful of clinical note summarizers.
[01:05] Ethan Cole: When you say deltas, are we talking token-level BLEU or our custom fidelity score?
[01:10] Dr. Lina Morales: It's the custom fidelity scoring, we weight hallucination penalty heavier — we saw fidelity drop from 0.92 to 0.83 on invoice set.
[01:20] Maya Patel: Ok that's pretty significant. Any infra notes? Were these runs on Redwood Dedicated or in the VPC pilot?
[01:28] Samir Rao: They were on the private VPC deployment with Redwood runtime — small chance it's environment-induced, but we flagged some KV cache thrash.
[01:36] Ethan Cole: Hmm, KV cache thrash — we saw similar before when sequence lengths spiked and batching pushed cache evictions. Might be a batch policy mismatch.
[01:45] Alex Chen: We did increase batch_size to 16 for throughput during that window, that could explain eviction.
[01:52] Maya Patel: Alright so possible contributors: prompt drift, batching/K-V cash (sic) behaviour, and model variant differences. We'll triage each.
[02:05] Dr. Lina Morales: Right — we tried a rollback to the previous model and got fidelity back up, so that's a strong signal it's model+prompt interactions.
[02:12] Samir Rao: But interestingly, some failures are non-deterministic — same prompt sometimes ok, sometimes malformed table outputs.
[02:22] Ethan Cole: That's classic partial-state KV cache or prefix mismatch. We'll try to reproduce with a minimal harness.
[02:30] Speaker 1: [inaudible] — is there any chance of tokenization mismatch when transferring prompts between systems?
[02:36] Maya Patel: Good question. We did see minor whitespace normalization differences; Ethan, can you check tokenizer logs?
[02:42] Ethan Cole: Yep, pulling tokenizer diff now — I'll check char-level normalization.
[02:46] Dr. Lina Morales: Also a note — our prompt set includes some user-provided examples with HTML snippets; could that perturb the model?
[02:54] Alex Chen: yes we found a subset where HTML tags caused truncated summaries.
[03:00] Maya Patel: Okay, so short list: 1) batch size induced KV evictions, 2) tokenizer/normalization differences, 3) prompt examples with HTML, 4) potential model variant mismatch.
[03:12] Ethan Cole: For the immediate patch I propose: 1) sweep prompt-set and escape HTML, 2) pin batch_size to 8 for the next run, 3) run 2k evals with scorecard v2.
[03:24] Priya Kapoor: From security: pinning is fine but we need to know if pinning affects throughput SLA — can you quantify cost/latency trade?
[03:33] Maya Patel: We'll include a short delta table — rough numbers — in the follow-up.
[03:37] Dr. Lina Morales: On guardrails — the false positives from the safety filter increased; are you filtering on hallucination signals or content categories?
[03:45] Ethan Cole: We're using a mix — content categories for PII and a separate hallucination heuristic that looks at token-level confidence. Might be too strict for some prompts.
[03:54] Samir Rao: We want to avoid over-blocking because the product team needs usable outputs. Alex, what's the tolerance?
[03:59] Alex Chen: Tolerance is low for false blocks on invoices — we need results for downstream parsers to work. So reduce filter aggressiveness on those sets.
[04:07] Maya Patel: Noted. We'll propose a per-route guardrail: whitelist invoice prompt IDs for relaxed hallucination thresholds.
[04:14] Dr. Lina Morales: That sounds good. Also, can Redwood run a targeted A/B with canary traffic to see guardrail impact?
[04:20] Ethan Cole: Yes, we can set up canary with 5% traffic on Dedicated pool, monitor quality and cost, then roll.
[04:27] Priya Kapoor: Make sure audit logs capture full inputs for compliance — we need retention notes.
[04:33] Maya Patel: We'll include retention policy details; default is 30 days for pilot but we can extend for enterprise.
[04:40] Samir Rao: For replicability, can you share the exact prompt normalization script?
[04:45] Ethan Cole: I'll share a gist with the normalization code and tokenizer diffs.
[04:50] Speaker 2: [crosstalk] sorry go ahead —
[04:52] Maya Patel: No worries — moving to prompt surgery specifics: we recommend three edits per failing prompt — stronger anchors, remove HTML, and add brief negative examples.
[05:03] Dr. Lina Morales: Can you show an example?
[05:06] Ethan Cole: Sure — take invoice-042: original prompt had 'extract line items' then big unstructured example — we add a clear schema header, and add 'do not hallucinate missing fields' as negative.
[05:20] Alex Chen: When you add negative examples, does that slow token generation? We worry about latency.
[05:26] Ethan Cole: Slightly, 2-8% added input token cost but should be within SLO if batching is adjusted.
[05:33] Maya Patel: We'll include a delta table in the follow-up showing latency/cost per prompt edit.
[05:39] Dr. Lina Morales: About scoring: the current fidelity is weighted too much on syntax — can we shift to semantic correctness for clinical prompts?
[05:48] Maya Patel: Yes we can produce alternate scoring profiles per route — Redwood supports per-route score configs.
[05:55] Samir Rao: Great. Also competitor note — we ran a baseline against Anthropic's endpoint and they didn't show the same hallucination pattern, but cost was higher.
[06:05] Maya Patel: That's useful context. We'll document tradeoffs.
[06:09] Ethan Cole: Re reproducing the flaky malformed table — I'll run a targeted harness that replicates sequence-length distributions and caching.
[06:18] Dr. Lina Morales: Please include the seed prompts that triggered the table bug, we uploaded a small set in the drive.
[06:24] Ethan Cole: Got it.
[06:26] [10 min mark skipped in transcription]
[16:35] Maya Patel: Back on — Ethan, any early reproductions?
[16:38] Ethan Cole: I ran a 500-sample reproduce run with batch_size 16 and saw similar tail failures; with batch_size 8 the tail almost disappears. So batching correlates.
[16:47] Alex Chen: Ok that's consistent with our perf tests. We can accept a moderate batch change.
[16:52] Priya Kapoor: From security, if batch changes require tuning autoscaler rules, we need documentation on how logs are shipped to our SIEM.
[16:59] Ethan Cole: We'll provide the autoscaler diff and a log-shipping config snippet.
[17:04] Dr. Lina Morales: On guardrails we also noticed the safety filter flagged some benign clinical abbreviations as PII. Can we add domain-specific allowlists?
[17:11] Maya Patel: Yes we support domain allowlists for tokens and regex patterns. We'll add the clinical list you provided as a starting point.
[17:18] Alex Chen: I'll push the allowlist file to the shared folder.
[17:22] Samir Rao: One open question: how will rollbacks be handled if the canary shows regressions — automatic rollback or manual?
[17:29] Ethan Cole: We recommend an automatic rollback threshold for severity > 0.1 fidelity drop or >3% error rate, but the customer can opt for manual.
[17:38] Maya Patel: Let's capture that as part of the fallback playbook. We'll send a draft.
[17:42] Dr. Lina Morales: Ok, timeline — we want v3 prompts and pin to batch_size 8 by Friday run, then 2k evals over the weekend.
[17:51] Maya Patel: Aiming for that. Any other blockers?
[17:55] Priya Kapoor: I need the KMS integration notes and the SSO cert for our security team review.
[18:00] Maya Patel: Noted — Priya we'll send that by Monday.
[18:03] Ethan Cole: Quick note — some of the degradation was amplified by longer context windows; we recommend trimming non-essential context in prompts where possible.
[18:12] Alex Chen: We can try that — we'll produce a trimmed prompt set as part of the 200-priority list.
[18:19] Dr. Lina Morales: A question on metrics: can Redwood push a per-prompt heatmap to our dashboard?
[18:25] Maya Patel: Yes we can export per-prompt metrics; we'll add a new view to your Console with fidelity by prompt ID.
[18:32] Samir Rao: Good. Also please include token-level cost breakdowns so we can justify Dedicated vs Hosted.
[18:38] Maya Patel: We'll include cost delta in the follow-up.
[18:42] Speaker 3: [inaudible]
[18:44] Maya Patel: Wrapping — recap and next steps.
[18:47] Maya Patel: 1) Redwood to send prompt-set v3 + scoring baseline (Maya) by 2026-07-23.
[18:54] Ethan Cole: 2) SE to run reproduce harness and share logs + tokenizer diffs (Ethan) by 2026-07-25.
[19:00] Alex Chen: 3) Customer to tag 200 priority prompts and run 2k evals (Alex/Lina) by 2026-07-29.
[19:07] Priya Kapoor: 4) Security to exchange SSO certs and KMS notes (Priya) by 2026-07-26.
[19:12] Maya Patel: 5) Schedule canary rollout and fallback drill for week of 2026-07-27 (Maya/Ethan/Samir).
[19:19] Dr. Lina Morales: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[19:22] Samir Rao: Thanks.
[19:25] Maya Patel: End.
